title: Talking About the Future in Norwegian
goal: Choose and form common Norwegian future expressions with skal, vil, kommer til å, and present tense.

objectives.statement: Choose and form common Norwegian future expressions with skal, vil, kommer til å, and present tense.

spans.value: Maja and Jonas are planning a short trip to Lillehammer. Some parts of the weekend are already arranged, while others depend on the weather.
Skal du gjøre noe i helga?

blocks.translation: Are you doing anything this weekend?

spans.value: Ja, jeg skal besøke søsteren min i Lillehammer. Vil du bli med?

blocks.translation: Yes, I’m going to visit my sister in Lillehammer. Do you want to come along?
I’d love to. When does the train leave?

spans.value: Det går fra Oslo klokka 08.12 på lørdag. Vi møtes på stasjonen kvart på åtte.

blocks.translation: It leaves Oslo at 8:12 on Saturday. We’ll meet at the station at quarter to eight.

spans.value: Det er tidlig! Men jeg skal kjøpe billetten i kveld.

blocks.translation: That’s early! But I’ll buy the ticket this evening.

spans.value: Bra. Jeg tror toget vil være ganske fullt.

blocks.translation: Good. I think the train will be quite full.

spans.value: Og se på værmeldingen. Det kommer til å regne hele lørdagen.

blocks.translation: And look at the weather forecast. It’s going to rain all day Saturday.

spans.value: Da tar jeg med regnjakke. På søndag blir det kanskje bedre.

blocks.translation: Then I’ll bring a rain jacket. On Sunday it may be better.

spans.value: The dialogue refers to the future in four different ways:

items.value: presents a plan, intention, or commitment.
can present a prediction, but it can also express desire or willingness.
presents an expected future result, often supported by present signs or circumstances.
can describe a scheduled or firmly arranged future event when the future context is clear.

spans.value: Norwegian therefore does not need one separate future tense for every future meaning. The form depends on how the speaker views the event.
when the subject has a plan, intention, agreement, or commitment.

no.value: Jeg skal besøke søsteren min på lørdag.

en.value: I’m going to visit my sister on Saturday.

no.value: Vi skal bo hos henne.

en.value: We’re going to stay with her.

no.value: Maja skal kjøpe billetten i kveld.

en.value: Maja is going to buy the ticket this evening.

no.value: Jeg skal ringe deg etter jobb.

en.value: I’ll call you after work.

spans.value: These sentences do more than locate an action in the future. They present it as decided or intended.

no.value: Jeg skal kjøpe billetten.

en.value: I’m going to buy the ticket.

no.value: Jeg skal å kjøpe billetten.

en.value: I’m going to buy the ticket.

no.value: Vi skal ikke reise på fredag.

en.value: We aren’t going to travel on Friday.

no.value: Skal du jobbe i morgen?

en.value: Are you going to work tomorrow?

no.value: Når skal dere reise?

en.value: When are you going to travel?

statement.value: when you want to present a future action as someone’s plan, intention, or commitment.

spans.value: does not always correspond to Norwegian
. For a decided first-person plan, Norwegian commonly uses

no.value: Jeg skal hente deg klokka seks.

en.value: I’ll pick you up at six.

no.value: Jeg vil hente deg klokka seks.

en.value: I want to pick you up at six.

spans.value: The second sentence can express desire or willingness rather than a neutral future plan.

sections.title: Scheduled and arranged events in the present tense

spans.value: Norwegian often uses the present tense for future events when a time expression or shared context makes the future meaning clear.

no.value: Toget går klokka 08.12 på lørdag.

en.value: The train leaves at 8:12 on Saturday.

no.value: Vi møtes på stasjonen kvart på åtte.

en.value: We’ll meet at the station at quarter to eight.

no.value: Kurset begynner neste uke.

en.value: The course begins next week.

no.value: Jeg reiser til Bergen i morgen.

en.value: I’m travelling to Bergen tomorrow.

spans.value: This use is especially common for timetables, appointments, and settled arrangements. Words such as
, and a future clock time prevent confusion with the present moment.

no.value: Vi skal møtes på stasjonen.

en.value: We’re going to meet at the station.

no.value: Vi møtes på stasjonen klokka 07.45.

en.value: We’ll meet at the station at 7:45.

spans.value: The first sentence highlights the plan. The second treats the meeting as an arranged event.
The difference is often one of perspective rather than objective fact. The same event can be described differently:

no.value: Jeg skal reise til Trondheim på mandag.

en.value: I’m going to travel to Trondheim on Monday.

no.value: Jeg reiser til Trondheim på mandag.

en.value: I’m travelling to Trondheim on Monday.

spans.value: emphasizes intention. The present-tense sentence presents the journey as settled.

sections.title: Common mistake: present tense without future context

spans.value: A present-tense form does not automatically mean future time.

no.value: Jeg jobber.

en.value: I’m working.

spans.value: Without a future expression or a clear shared arrangement, this normally refers to the present.

no.value: Jeg jobber i morgen.

en.value: I’m working tomorrow.

spans.value: for a prediction or assessment about the future, especially when it reflects an opinion, calculation, or general expectation.

no.value: Jeg tror toget vil være fullt.

en.value: I think the train will be full.

no.value: Prisene vil stige neste år.

en.value: Prices will rise next year.

no.value: Det vil ta omtrent tre timer.

en.value: It will take about three hours.

no.value: Turen vil bli lettere med godt utstyr.

en.value: The trip will become easier with good equipment.

no.value: Det vil regne senere.

en.value: It will rain later.

no.value: Det vil å regne senere.

en.value: It will rain later.

no.value: Det vil ikke ta lang tid.

en.value: It won’t take long.

spans.value: often makes the predictive meaning clear:

no.value: Jeg tror været vil bli bedre på søndag.

en.value: I think the weather will improve on Sunday.

no.value: Jeg vil reise til Lillehammer.

en.value: I want to travel to Lillehammer.

no.value: Jeg vil hjelpe deg.

en.value: I want to help you. / I’m willing to help you.

no.value: Jeg skal reise til Lillehammer på lørdag.

en.value: I’m going to travel to Lillehammer on Saturday.

spans.value: For a prediction, make the predictive context clear:

no.value: Jeg tror Maja vil like Lillehammer.

en.value: I think Maja will like Lillehammer.

spans.value: can never refer to a person’s future action. The important issue is possible ambiguity. If you mean a plan,

sections.title: Expected results with kommer til å

spans.value: for an expected future event or result. It is especially natural when present information, visible signs, or known circumstances point toward that result.

no.value: Det kommer til å regne hele lørdagen.

en.value: It’s going to rain all day Saturday.

no.value: Toget kommer til å bli fullt.

en.value: The train is going to be full.

no.value: Vi kommer til å trenge regnjakker.

en.value: We’re going to need rain jackets.

no.value: Hun kommer til å bli glad når vi kommer.

en.value: She’s going to be happy when we arrive.

spans.value: carries the present-tense ending. The main verb remains in the infinitive.

no.value: Det kommer til å snø.

en.value: It’s going to snow.

no.value: De kommer til å vente lenge.

en.value: They’re going to wait a long time.

no.value: Det kommer ikke til å snø.

en.value: It isn’t going to snow.

no.value: Det kommer til å regne.

en.value: It’s going to rain.

no.value: Det kommer regne.

en.value: It’s going to rain.

spans.value: Both forms can make predictions. A useful A2-level distinction is:

items.value: often presents a prediction as an opinion, assessment, or neutral forecast.
often presents an expected result, particularly when circumstances or signs point toward it.

no.value: Jeg tror toget vil være fullt.

en.value: I think the train will be full.

no.value: Se på køen! Toget kommer til å bli fullt.

en.value: Look at the queue! The train is going to be full.

spans.value: The visible queue supports the prediction.

no.value: Ekspertene tror prisene vil stige.

en.value: The experts think prices will rise.

no.value: Med disse nye kostnadene kommer prisene til å stige.

en.value: With these new costs, prices are going to rise.

spans.value: This is a useful tendency, not an absolute boundary. In everyday Norwegian, both expressions can sometimes fit. The speaker chooses how to frame the prediction.
The same general situation can support all four expressions.

no.value: Jeg skal kjøpe togbilletten i kveld.

en.value: I’m going to buy the train ticket this evening.

no.value: Vi møtes på Oslo S klokka 07.45.

en.value: We’ll meet at Oslo Central Station at 7:45.

no.value: Jeg tror reisen vil ta omtrent to timer.

en.value: I think the journey will take about two hours.

spans.value: An expected result based on signs

no.value: Det kommer til å bli en våt helg.

en.value: It’s going to be a wet weekend.

en.value: The bus is leaving. / The bus goes.

prompt.value: Message Maja about the library open house tomorrow: Jonas has promised to set out the chairs before the guests arrive. The library opens at 11. Maja thinks many families will come. Dark clouds are gathering, and rain is forecast. Write a message. Tell her about the plan, the opening time, Maja's expectation, and what the weather suggests. Use natural future forms and write your own sentences.

payload.judge_prompt: Check the response against the supplied facts and requested perspectives. Accept natural Bokmål variants rather than requiring one exact future form for each fact: skal can express the promise, present tense can report the fixed opening time, and both vil and kommer til å can express predictions when the surrounding wording makes the intended perspective clear. Do not treat a natural alternative as wrong solely because it uses a different future expression. Require the message to distinguish the settled plan, timetable, opinion-based expectation, and evidence-based expectation.

criteria.instruction: Writes a connected, practical Norwegian update to Maja about the library open house.
Accurately includes Jonas's promise, the library's 11.00 opening, Maja's expectation of many families, and the rain outlook.
Makes clear which event is planned, scheduled, expected as Maja's view, and suggested by the current weather signs, using natural future wording for each.
Is comprehensible Norwegian despite minor errors.
